content:
Nikhil Sharma: For the staged rollout, can we enumerate exactly what has to be “green” before we go from hosted subset -> broader default? Need a list we can point to in go/no-go.

Marissa Cole: +1. Also clarify what’s “page vs ticket” so we don’t block on non-paging noise.

Sean Gallagher: From SRE side: we need objective gates. Suggest grouping by (1) perf canary, (2) error budget + incidents, (3) observability, (4) support/docs readiness.

Aditya Rao: Agree. Can we make sure we include unit economics? Like $/1K tokens delta doesn’t have to be perfect for launch, but should be non-negative for standard/cost-efficient on top workloads.

Henry Cho: Also: what’s the required docs state? merged to public docs + console copy? and SDK params released?

Connor O'Brien: Release-wise: I need an explicit checklist for “train makes it” vs “launch gate”. (Some things can miss 1.22 but still be ok behind flag.)

Nikhil Sharma: Cool. Drafting a list here. Please nitpick.

Nikhil Sharma: Proposed launch criteria (expand rollout %):
- Perf canary: pass rate + tail constraints
- SLO/error budget: no material burn increase
- Metrics/dashboards: tier dimension stable, no cardinality blowups
- Support readiness: macros + runbook + known issues
- Docs: public docs + API/SDK examples
- Rollback: kill switch tested

Allison Grant: Perf canary specifics matter. For gating we should tie to the new perf-canary rules: fast tier p99, standard p95. Also need “baseline refresh” process noted so we don’t block on stale baselines.

Rafael Mendes: +1. For rollout expansion we should require N consecutive green canary windows. We can set N=3 (each 30m) for early stage, then N=12 (6h) for widening.

Aisha Bello: SLO/error budget:
- For hosted regions in rollout: 24h p99 for fast tier within target (or within +X% of pre-rollout), and p95 for standard within target.
- Error budget burn rate <= 1.0x week-over-week for those routes/models.
- No new SEV-2+ attributed to batching defaults.

Sean Gallagher: I’d phrase as: “no breach of paging SLOs, and burn rate within guardrails.” Also explicitly: fast tier should not increase request timeouts / cancellations.

Lauren Bishop: For Dedicated: before we allow opt-in for broader set of Dedicated tenants:
- Override precedence verified (customer override > route policy > tier default)
- Tenant-level effective config visible in Console (or at least via API)
- Capacity variability: make sure standard tier doesn’t cause queue blowups under burst.

Vanessa Ortiz: Fleet/capacity gate: if we’re enabling cost-efficient more broadly, make sure autoscaling guardrails are configured. Otherwise we’ll “save $/token” and then run into head-of-line blocking.

Elliot Price: Docs gate proposal:
- Docs PR merged + published: “SLO tiers (fast/standard/cost-efficient)”, “what happens if I don’t pick a tier”, “how to override”, “troubleshooting latency regressions”.
- Include clear statement: tier selection changes batching behavior only (no logging/data handling changes).

Wei Chen: SDK/API gate:
- Python + TS SDKs: tier parameter/header documented.
- Examples repo updated with migration snippet.
- If SDK release lags, we can still launch via header, but docs must show both.

Kira Thompson: Support readiness:
- Support playbook updated w/ decision tree: confirm effective tier -> check region -> check streaming -> recommend moving to fast vs setting per-route override.
- Known issues list (e.g., “fast tier on model X in region Y: watch p99”) so support doesn’t reinvent.

ReleaseBot: (auto) runtime-1.22 branch cut scheduled for Thu 10:00 PT. Feature flags default OFF unless explicitly enabled in rollout config.

Connor O'Brien: Rollback gate should include: kill switch works AND we’ve practiced rollback in staging w/ dashboards confirming tier labels disappear / revert.

Allison Grant: Observability/cardinality:
- Tier label present on latency + queue metrics AND cardinality controls enabled.
- Telemetry cost stable (no >20% increase in metrics ingestion for runtime namespace) during canary.
- Dashboard panels verified: breakdown by tier/model/region actually renders (no missing labels).

Rafael Mendes: Perf canary gate proposal (concrete):
- perf-canary suite for top N models in 2 primary regions: >= 98% pass over last 50 runs.
- No regression > 5% in fast p99 vs baseline; no regression > 3% in standard p95.
- Decode throughput for cost-efficient: >= baseline (or justify with queueing tradeoff). If it’s worse, we pause.

Sean Gallagher: Add overload behavior gate:
- When load > capacity, we see expected backpressure (429 / queue admission) rather than tail latency cliff.
- Alerting routes correctly: fast-tier p99 breach pages; standard/cost-efficient creates ticket (unless broad).

Aditya Rao: On cost: we can set a “non-blocking but track” metric:
- Standard tier: target 8–15% throughput gain on representative workload mix.
- Cost-efficient tier: target 15–30% throughput gain.
If we’re below target but SLOs are good, we can still launch behind flag but we shouldn’t call it a win in comms.

Henry Cho: Also add “reason codes present + sampled traces”: if customers ask “why did it pick this profile?”, we need to be able to answer.

Nikhil Sharma: Great. Summarizing final “must be green” list for hosted broader default:
1) Perf canary
- >=98% pass (last 50 runs) on top models/regions
- fast: p99 <= baseline +5% (or within SLO target, whichever stricter)
- standard: p95 <= baseline +3% (or within SLO target)
2) SLO / error budget
- 24h burn rate <= 1.0x pre-rollout for impacted routes
- no increase in timeouts/cancels; no SEV-2+ attributed
3) Observability
- tier-labeled metrics live + dashboards validated
- ingestion/cost stable (no >20% jump); cardinality guardrails ON
4) Support readiness
- playbook + macros updated; known-issues section published internally
5) Docs/SDKs
- public docs merged + published; examples updated
- SDK param shipped OR header-only path documented clearly
6) Safety
- feature flag + kill switch verified in staging; rollback runbook linked

Nikhil Sharma: Dedicated opt-in has the above + Lauren’s precedence/visibility requirements.

Lauren Bishop: Looks good. For Dedicated I’ll add one more: confirm override audit logs (who changed what) are visible for the tenant.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Please include explicit “pager health”: no open paging alerts in the tier dashboards at go/no-go time.

Elliot Price: I’ll make sure docs checklist includes the “FAQ: if I don’t pick a tier, what happens?” and “How to force fast tier for streaming routes” since support keeps getting that.

Connor O'Brien: Can you paste this into the launch brief + rollout checklist doc? I’ll link it in the release train notes.

Nikhil Sharma: Yep, I’ll drop into the launch brief + pin this thread. Thanks all.
